messages:
taylor: Heads-up — saw a batch of user reports about higher p99 for APAC customers this morning. Metrics show many requests still hitting us-west instead of ap-southeast.
maya: Hmm, that's likely the region selector probed wrong or probe TTL expired. Any logs from the router? :eyes:
sanjay: Router logs show probe latency for ap-southeast spiked ~06:10 but health checks still marked healthy until 06:20.
taylor: That aligns with some bad probe smoothing. We should bias selection by observed latency per tenant and also respect customer tier (enterprise vs free). Right now we only do static geo preference + recent probes.
julie: Agree — plus we need a graceful model-variant fallback. If nearest region is overloaded, prefer a smaller/quantized variant in-region over routing cross-continent to keep latency low.
liam: Can we design priority: 1) same-region same-tier model, 2) same-region smaller-variant, 3) tier-favored nearby-region primary-model, 4) remote fallback? That would avoid cross-continent hops.
maya: Sounds good. Also add a cost/quota check: reserved capacity customers should never be sent to a lower-quality variant without explicit rollout flag.
sanjay: Right — reserved capacity and dedicated customers must have a hard override. For hosted tiers, we can be more aggressive with fallback.
taylor: Here's a sketch of a routing rule I made for discussion:

```
prefer_region_by_latency: true
latency_threshold_ms: 150
tier_overrides:
  enterprise:
    enforce_same_region: true
    allow_variant_fallback: false
  standard:
    enforce_same_region: false
    allow_variant_fallback: true
fallback_order:
  - same_region: smaller_variant
  - nearby_region: same_variant
  - remote_region: smaller_variant
```

julie: That YAML is useful. Two questions: how do we compute "nearby_region"? Based on RTT probe bucket + geo distance? And how does console show what was chosen for each request for debugging?
liam: For nearby we can use tiered buckets: <50ms local, 50-150ms nearby, >150ms remote. We already store probe RTT per region per POP in telemetry. Console can surface last-chosen-region + probe RTT + variant via the trace explorer.
maya: Telemetry note: we must emit routing decision events with fields: tenant_id, tier, request_id, probe_rtt_map (stringified), chosen_region, chosen_variant, reason_code. That will help evals and audits.
taylor: Good. Also UX on rollouts: in-console rollout page should show a preview of routing impact when you enable "allow_variant_fallback" for a tenant group. Maybe simulate 1h traffic and show % that would have been routed remote vs variant.
sanjay: Implementation concern: routing in the hot path must be cheap. Precompute per-tenant routing policy object with ranked region/variant list updated on probe updates. No heavy aggregation per request.
julie: Ops question: what about model-consistency for streaming chat tokens? If we switch variant mid-stream for fallback, that breaks KV cache.
liam: We must never switch model mid-session. Fallback only allowed at request start. For streaming sessions, if region becomes unavailable mid-stream, use server-side retry to same-region smaller-variant if KV-compatible, else return a graceful error and metrics.
aylor: (typo) — taylor: Good catch.
ops-bot: incident: #INC-2026-APAC-LATENCY created by taylor at 2026-03-20T06:25Z
deploy-bot: canary: routing-policy-service v2.3.1 deployed to canary-pop at 06:40 — auto-tests passed :white_check_mark:
maya: Action items: 1) sanjay to add per-tenant ranked region/variant precompute (ETA 2w). 2) liam to extend telemetry with decision events (ETA 3d). 3) julie to add rollback/preview in console (ETA 1w). 4) taylor to draft runbook for mid-stream failures (ETA 3d).
sanjay: I'll open PR for precompute design and include complexity/cost analysis.
liam: I'll add the event schema to the telemetry repo and a small dashboard showing "variant fallback rate by region".
julie: I'll mock the console preview UI and send screenshots in product-review.
taylor: Thanks team — let's sync tomorrow 09:30 PT. If anyone finds an urgent regression, ping #oncall and escalate.
